location: Sections 1.2 and 1.3 (pp. 5-6); Sections 2 onward not read

title: The Euclidean plane cannot be colored with five colors
problem: Every five-coloring of the Euclidean plane has a monochromatic unit-distance pair, so the chromatic number of the plane is six or seven.
method: Transfer an arbitrary proper coloring to a weak measurable coloring by compactness and an invariant probability on characters of the algebraic plane, then rule out five labels with a Furstenberg-Zimmer rigidity argument and a cycle argument on connected exclusion sets.

title: Erdos's reciprocal-sum conjecture and quasipolynomial Szemeredi bounds
problem: Every set of positive integers with divergent reciprocal sum contains arithmetic progressions of every finite length, with a quasipolynomial bound on k-progression-free subsets of {1,...,N}.

title: Superexponential van der Waerden numbers
problem: The van der Waerden number W_r(k) exceeds k^{ck floor(log_2 r)} for all r at least 2 and large k, so W_r(k)^{1/k} tends to infinity.

title: Counterexamples to Sidorenko's conjecture and the forcing conjecture
problem: A connected bipartite graph on 35 vertices and 66 edges has a homomorphism density below the Sidorenko bound in some host graph, and the same graph disproves the Skokan-Thoma forcing conjecture.

title: Counterexamples to Ryser's covering conjecture
problem: For every sufficiently large prime q there is an intersecting (q+1)-partite (q+1)-uniform hypergraph with covering number q+1, which disproves Ryser's conjecture.
method: unclear from abstract (the abstract mentions an explicit construction over prime and extension fields)

title: Hindman's finite sums and products conjecture
field: Ramsey theory, combinatorics of the integers
problem: Every finite coloring of the positive integers contains k-element sets whose nonempty subset sums and nonempty subset products all share one color.

title: The Harary-Hill and Zarankiewicz crossing-number formulas
problem: The crossing numbers of complete graphs and complete bipartite graphs equal the classical formulas, so the classical drawings are optimal among plane drawings with continuous edge arcs.

title: The higher-dimensional Erdos distinct-distances conjecture
problem: Any n distinct points in R^d for fixed d at least 3 determine at least c_d n^{2/d} distinct distances.

title: Planar distinct distances and unit-distance bounds
problem: All but o(n) points of an n-point planar set determine at least n^{1-eps} distinct nonzero distances, and the number of unit-distance pairs is O(n^{4/3-delta}).

title: Combinatorial invariance of Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials
problem: Isomorphic Bruhat intervals in arbitrary Coxeter systems have identical equal-parameter Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials.

title: Shareshian-Wachs elementary positivity
problem: The chromatic quasisymmetric function of every natural unit interval graph has elementary-basis coefficients in N[q].
method: unclear from abstract (the coefficients are counted by explicitly described permutations)

title: Sharp logarithmic exponents for off-diagonal Ramsey numbers
problem: The off-diagonal Ramsey number r(5,t) equals t^4 / (log t)^{3+o(1)}, which fixes the logarithmic exponent and matches the classical upper bound at that scale; a companion paper extends this to every fixed s at least 6.
method: Upper bound from uniform independent sets and random sampling; lower bound from a K_5-free graph on incidence pairs (point, hyperplane) of PG(4,q), where a long independent sequence in each random stream yields a consistent flag tuple whose conditional entropy, compressed along a balanced tree of incidence tests with a sparse-pair description theorem, contradicts the entropy lower bound.
location: Section 1.2 (p. 3) proof overview; Section 2 (p. 4) upper bound; Sections 3 to 11 not read

title: The hypercube Ramsey number has linear order
problem: The two-color Ramsey number of the n-dimensional binary cube is at most C 2^n for an absolute constant C.
method: Reduce a counterexample to two host sides of size N, bound patch discrepancy with density gains and width budgets, then embed the cube by allocating subcubes to patches and obtain distinct labels by Hall's condition on random two-element subsets of common-neighbourhood sets.

title: Classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations
problem: A finite point configuration is monochromatic at its original scale in every finite coloring of high-dimensional Euclidean space exactly when a tensor condition over its coordinate field holds.
method: Criterion stated as a necessary and sufficient tensor condition over the coordinate field (proof method unclear from abstract).

title: Seymour's second-neighborhood conjecture
problem: Every nonempty finite oriented graph has a vertex with at least as many vertices at directed distance two as at directed distance one.

title: Deterministic construction of strong thin spanning trees
problem: Every loopless k-edge-connected multigraph has a spanning tree that meets each cut in at most C/k of the cut's edges, and such a tree can be found in polynomial time.
method: unclear from abstract (the abstract claims a deterministic polynomial-time construction)

title: Talagrand's expectation thresholds, discrete convexity, and graph decompositions
problem: Integral and fractional expectation thresholds agree up to a universal factor, and every graph's edges split into a boundedly many pieces with controlled containment thresholds.

title: The second Kahn-Kalai conjecture
problem: The threshold for G(n,p) to contain a copy of H is at most C p_E(n,H)(1 + log_2 h) for a universal constant C.

title: Bounded-degree coboundary expanders in every dimension
problem: For every d at least 3 there are arbitrarily large d-dimensional complexes with bounded vertex degrees and uniform F_2 coboundary expansion in every degree below d.

title: Deterministic nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs in every fixed degree
problem: For every fixed d at least 3 and every sufficiently large even n, a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm outputs a simple nonbipartite d-regular Ramanujan graph.

title: The circulant Hadamard and Barker-sequence conjectures
problem: Real circulant Hadamard matrices exist only in orders 1 and 4, so Barker sequences of length above one exist exactly at lengths 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 11, 13.

title: Barnette's Hamiltonian-cycle conjecture
problem: Every finite simple cubic 3-vertex-connected bipartite planar graph has a Hamiltonian cycle.
method: unclear from abstract (the title names paired states, which is not explained in the abstract)

title: The Erdos-Gallai cycle-decomposition conjecture
problem: The edges of every simple graph on n vertices split into at most Cn simple cycles and single edges, for an absolute constant C.

title: Power savings for intersective polynomial differences and prime arguments
problem: A set avoiding nonzero differences h(1), h(2), ... for an intersective polynomial h of degree k has size O_h(N^{1-c_k}), with c_k depending only on the degree, and a power saving also holds at prime arguments under a unit-root condition.
method: unclear from abstract (the prime-argument case uses a zero-free half-plane theorem for Dirichlet L-functions)

title: Power savings for planar halving lines and k-sets
problem: A planar set with no three collinear has O(n^{4/3-eps}) halving pairs and O(n(k+1)^{1/3-eps}) strictly separable k-subsets, with nonquantitative constants.

title: Correspondence coloring with a fixed forbidden subgraph
problem: Every K_r-free graph of large maximum degree has correspondence chromatic number O_r(Delta / log Delta), and K_r-free graphs of average degree d have independent sets of size Omega_r(n log d / d).
method: Random rounds that activate each available entry with probability proportional to a weight, with a potential that combines an entropy term, a penalty for lost weight, and the incident edge mass, and a vertex-splitting step that controls triangle mass so the Lovasz local lemma holds in all rounds at once.
location: Section 1.2 (p. 4) proof overview; Section 3 (contents) for vertex splitting, not read

title: Counterexamples to infinite matroid intersection and packing/covering
problem: Two self-dual partitional matroids on a countably infinite ground set admit neither a packing/covering partition nor an intersection witness, in ZFC.
method: unclear from abstract (the examples are explicit)

title: Uniform influence and sharp thresholds for graph and hypergraph properties
problem: Relabeling-invariant increasing properties of graphs and r-uniform hypergraphs cross from probability epsilon to 1 - epsilon within width O((log n)^{-2}) for graphs and O_r((log n)^{-r/(r-1)}) for hypergraphs.

title: Snaky in 21 Maker moves
problem: Maker can claim the six-cell Snaky hexomino within 21 Maker moves on the infinite square board against arbitrary Breaker play.
method: unclear from abstract (the abstract states that Maker can confine its claims to a fixed 251-cell board)

title: The sharp terminal leave in random triangle removal
problem: Starting from K_n and deleting uniformly chosen triangles, the number of terminal edges divided by n^{3/2} converges in L^2 to 1/(2 sqrt 2).

title: Cycle-clique Ramsey numbers
problem: R(C_m, K_n) = (m-1)(n-1)+1 for all m at least n at least 3, except R(C_3, K_3) = 6.
method: Expansion in a minimal counterexample, a large-clique lemma, and an optimization of paths joining clique vertices reduce the remaining cases to 3,099 parameter-pattern instances, which two exact implementations of proved inference rules exclude, with deduction traces supplied.

title: Polynomial removal fails for ordered binary matrices
problem: A fixed 66 by 66 binary pattern has no polynomial bound for ordered matrix removal.
method: unclear from abstract (the abstract describes an explicit pattern construction)

title: A power improvement in the Heilbronn triangle lower bound
problem: For large n there are n points in the unit square with every determined triangle of area at least c_1 n^{-2+eta}, so the almost n^{-2} upper bound is false.

title: Boolean functions violate the square-root degree bound by arbitrary factors
problem: For every C > 0 there is a sign-valued Boolean function whose linear Fourier coefficients sum to more than C times the square root of its degree, which refutes the Gopalan-Servedio conjecture.

title: Serre's intersection-multiplicity conjecture
problem: Serre's intersection multiplicity is strictly positive for nonzero finitely generated modules over a regular local ring when the tensor product has finite length and the dimensions are complementary.

title: Lech's multiplicity conjecture
problem: Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity does not decrease under a flat local homomorphism of nonzero Noetherian local rings, in every dimension and characteristic.

title: A counterexample to the small Cohen–Macaulay module conjecture
problem: A three-dimensional complete Noetherian normal local domain over C has no nonzero finitely generated maximal Cohen–Macaulay module, disproving the domain form of the conjecture.

title: A counterexample to Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture
problem: A finitely presented torsion-free group G has F_2[G] with nonzero zero divisors, and G has a finite two-dimensional classifying space.

title: A torsion-free group algebra that is not directly finite
field: group rings, sofic groups, cellular automata
problem: A finitely presented torsion-free nonsofic group has an F_2 group algebra that is not directly finite, with companion counterexamples to surjunctivity and to the unrestricted group-ring determinant conjecture.

title: A counterexample to finitistic-dimension finiteness
problem: A finite-dimensional complex algebra has finite-dimensional modules of unbounded finite projective dimension, disproving the little finitistic dimension conjecture.

title: Counterexamples to Auslander–Reiten, Tachikawa and related homological conjectures
problem: Finite-dimensional algebras over F_2(q,H_1,H_2) disprove the Auslander–Reiten, Gorenstein-projective and Tachikawa second conjectures, and an associated endomorphism algebra disproves several Nakayama-type conjectures.
method: Builds an explicit algebra over a characteristic-two rational function field, then passes to an associated endomorphism algebra to get the Nakayama-type counterexamples.

title: Eisenbud–Green–Harris and lex-plus-powers
problem: Over any characteristic-zero field, every homogeneous ideal containing a regular sequence of degree at least two has a lex-plus-powers ideal with the same Hilbert function and no smaller graded Betti numbers.

title: A counterexample to Kurosh's division-ring problem
problem: A countable characteristic-zero division ring is algebraic over its center and generated by two elements over it, yet has infinite dimension over the center.

title: The blockwise Alperin weight conjecture
problem: For every finite group and every prime p, each p-block has as many irreducible Brauer characters as it has conjugacy classes of weights.

title: Donovan's conjecture over fields and complete mixed-characteristic DVRs
problem: Blocks with bounded defect group order have finitely many Morita equivalence classes over each algebraically closed field of characteristic p and over each complete mixed-characteristic DVR with algebraically closed residue field.

title: Tensor saturation for even spin groups
problem: For Spin(2n), n≥2, an invariant at a positive integral dilation of three dominant weights summing into the root lattice gives an invariant at the original weights.

title: Saxl's conjecture and universal tensor squares
problem: The tensor square of every staircase representation contains every irreducible representation of the symmetric group, and every S_n with n not in {2,4,9} has an irreducible whose tensor square contains all irreducibles.
method: unclear from abstract (one companion title refers to a cyclic polytabloid proof; the abstract text does not describe it)

title: Finite lattice representation and undecidability
problem: Some finite lattices are not congruence lattices of finite algebras, and no algorithm decides representability or recognizes full subgroup intervals of finite groups.
method: Characterizes the representable finite lattices by an explicit colored-graph criterion, then proves that deciding the criterion is undecidable.

title: The ℓ¹-Bass conjecture for all discrete groups
problem: For every discrete group, Hattori–Stallings traces of idempotent matrices over ℓ¹(G) are supported on finitely many conjugacy classes of finite-order elements.

title: Finite symmetric tensor categories and the Verlinde tower
problem: Every finite symmetric tensor category over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0 has an exact faithful strong monoidal fiber functor to a higher Verlinde category, including in characteristic two.

title: Integral counterexamples to Gersten's conjecture
problem: Two two-dimensional ramified regular local rings of mixed characteristic (0,5) have nonzero integral K_3 or K_5 classes that vanish over their fraction fields.

title: Foulkes' conjecture for sixth powers and quadratic stabilization
problem: Sym^6(Sym^b V) embeds equivariantly in Sym^b(Sym^6 V) for b≥6, and the canonical map Sym^b(Sym^a V) to Sym^a(Sym^b V) is surjective for a≥2 and b≥a(a−1).

title: The geometric phase diagram, diffusion, and spectra of random planar maps
problem: Critical FK planar maps converge to LQG spheres for 0<q≤4 and to the Brownian continuum random tree for q>4, and stationary walks on FK-Ising and spanning-tree maps converge to Liouville Brownian motion.
method: Stationary random walk that chooses uniformly among incident half-edges, time-accelerated by the edge count, is identified in the limit using stated Brownian and LQG inputs.

title: Planar first-passage geometry and the absence of bigeodesics
problem: Planar first-passage percolation has no doubly infinite geodesic when the minimum of four weights has finite second moment, and the exponential limit shape is strictly convex with C1 boundary.

title: Critical percolation on every quasi-transitive graph
problem: At the critical probability, bond percolation on every infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph with p_c<1 has no infinite cluster, and bond and site percolation on Z^3 have none either.
method: For Z^3 the abstract names a finite connection inequality for independent hyperedges, a finite-scale extension estimate and an adaptive exploration; the general graph method is not stated.

title: The Benjamini–Schramm nonuniqueness conjecture
problem: Every infinite connected locally finite nonamenable quasi-transitive graph has a nonempty interval of p with infinitely many infinite clusters, and p_c<p_{2→2}≤p_u.

title: Canonical O(3) continuum limit and exact O(4) mass asymptotics
problem: The 2D O(3) model has a canonical massive continuum limit, the square-lattice O(4) model has an exact low-temperature mass asymptotic, and O(n) spin correlations decay exponentially for n≥3 at every positive temperature.

title: Critical and near-critical XY scaling and BKT universality
problem: For the square-lattice cosine XY model, the critical axis correlation decays as r^{-1/4}(log r)^{1/8}, and the correlation length has a BKT essential singularity.

title: The low-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick fluctuation law
problem: For zero-field Gaussian SK at every β>1, the log partition function has variance asymptotic to c_β n^{1/3}, with full-sequence convergence of a centered and standardized law.

title: Conformal universality for weakly interacting and random-bond Ising models
problem: Weak even multispin perturbations preserve critical bulk spin and energy limits, and weak contour interactions and weak iid bond disorder give chordal SLE3 interface limits.

title: GOE bulk universality for regular graphs with weak Anderson disorder
problem: The bulk adjacency eigenvalue process of a uniform random d-regular graph (d≥3) converges to the GOE law, and the same holds under weak iid diagonal disorder.

title: Directional zero–one laws beyond iid environments and iid ballisticity
problem: On Z^d (d≥3) directional escape has probability zero or one under iid strictly elliptic and finite-range-dependent ergodic environments, and a.s. directional transience implies ballisticity in iid uniformly elliptic environments.

title: The Mézard–Parisi formula for diluted spin glasses
problem: For Poisson-diluted even-arity Ising models in the Panchenko–Talagrand class, the limiting free energy equals the infimum over finite-depth hierarchical trial laws.

title: Perceptron free energies and microscopic jamming exponents
problem: Variational free energies are found for Ising and spherical perceptrons at every positive density, and at margin −1 a sharp feasibility threshold with gap and force exponents is identified.
method: The companion jamming paper pins its exponent intervals with a finite numerical certificate that carries mathematical error bounds.

title: Random-cluster interfaces: critical, disordered, thermal, and natural-time scaling
problem: Critical square-lattice FK interfaces converge to chordal SLE_κ for 0<q≤4, and complete nested loop collections converge to CLE_κ for 1≤q≤4.

title: Critical and quenched near-critical universality for Poisson–Voronoi percolation
problem: Cardy's formula holds for annealed critical Poisson–Voronoi crossings, and near-critical crossing thresholds converge in probability to the triangular-lattice law.
method: Cardy's crossing formula is taken as an input, and near-critical thresholds are compared to the triangular lattice through the monotone coupling.

title: Gaussian free field limits throughout the balanced six-vertex regime
problem: The height function of the balanced square-lattice six-vertex model with 0<c≤2 converges to a Gaussian free field with variance multiplier 1/arcsin(c/2).
method: The plane state is defined as a limit over balanced tori; the abstract does not describe the estimates.

title: The double-dimer loop ensemble converges to CLE4
problem: The complete double-dimer loop ensemble on the half-plane Temperleyan square lattice converges to nested CLE4, matching each macroscopic loop as an unparametrized curve.

title: Critical SK autocorrelation processes and dynamics across the temperature transition
problem: Heat-bath dynamics of zero-field SK has cutoff on the log n scale for β<1, mixing time n^{2/3+o(1)} at β=1, and stretched-exponential mixing from a fixed Gibbs start for β>1.

title: Continuum phase transitions for radial pair potentials
problem: Stable radial pair potentials in three dimensions produce a first-order transition, a derivative jump of the free energy, at one inverse temperature throughout an open density interval.
method: Explicit potential construction (a divergent core, then a bounded continuous potential with algebraic tail), with the free energy jump shown for each; the abstract does not name the estimates.

title: Exact three- and four-state reconstruction thresholds and four-state tree capacity
field: broadcast on trees, stochastic block models
problem: The reconstruction threshold dλ²>1 is exact for 3-state symmetric and 4-state ferromagnetic Potts broadcast on regular and Poisson trees, giving the exact weak-recovery threshold for the symmetric three-community SBM.
method: Polynomial inequalities are checked in exact rational arithmetic for the four-state case, and an L3 capacity with edge resistances λ^{-2|e|} gives an exact test on general bounded-degree trees.

title: Exact Hausdorff gauges for SLE
problem: The explicit gauge r^d (log log 1/r)^{(2−d)/2}, with d=1+κ/8, gives positive finite measure to every nontrivial positive-time trace segment of chordal SLE_κ for 0<κ<8.

title: The free uniform spanning forest is a factor of IID
field: probability on graphs, factors of IID
problem: The free uniform spanning forest of every infinite connected locally finite simple graph is a factor of independent vertex labels, and invariant strongly Rayleigh processes on countable groups are factors of IID too.
method: One isomorphism-equivariant Borel rule, using no root, maps independent vertex labels to the forest.

title: Gaussian fields and interfaces for triangular-lattice Lipschitz heights
problem: Triangular-lattice Lipschitz height models converge to Gaussian free fields, and at a tuned boundary amplitude the uniform real-height interface converges to chordal SLE4.
method: Reflection positivity, a spectral sum rule and boundary comparison against Gaussian moment identities.

title: The joint critical Ashkin–Teller current limit
problem: On the critical Ashkin–Teller line, the height and both current-cluster collections converge jointly to a Gaussian free field and to canonical recursive local sets of that field.

title: All-temperature pressure of orthogonally invariant Ising spin glasses
problem: For Ising spin glasses with Haar-random eigenvectors and compactly supported spectra, the limiting pressure at every fixed temperature equals an explicit variational formula, and the zero-field ground-state energy follows as temperature tends to zero.

title: Limiting random SAT thresholds, sharp variance and computability
problem: Random k-SAT has a finite positive limiting satisfiability threshold for every k≥3, a hitting-time variance of order Θ_k(n), and the 3-SAT threshold is a computable real.
method: Concentration of a capped last-satisfiable index with a comparison across system sizes gives the threshold; for computability, a deletion estimate gives lower certificates and a finite hierarchical approximation of the soft pressure gives upper certificates.

title: The exact factor-of-IID threshold for free Ising spins on trees
field: probability on trees, factors of IID
problem: The free zero-field ferromagnetic Ising measure on the d-regular tree (d≥3) is a factor of IID exactly when tanh β ≤ (d−1)^{-1/2}, including equality.
method: A root-free spin construction that is almost surely equivariant under each tree automorphism; the abstract gives no further detail.

title: The three-quarter exponent for honeycomb self-avoiding walk
problem: A uniform n-step self-avoiding walk on the honeycomb lattice has diameter n^{3/4+o(1)}, and its local mass and covering numbers scale with exponent 4/3.
method: unclear from abstract (companion titles mention radial transfer estimates and polygon length laws)

title: Optimal logarithmic mixing of the Thorp shuffle
problem: The Thorp shuffle mixes 2^d labeled cards in Θ(log N) physical shuffles, in total variation from the worst initial deck, for the whole permutation.
method: After a fixed number of deterministic coordinate sweeps, bounds on partially observed permutation laws in random coordinate frames, plus a Fourier transfer, control the full permutation law (per the companion abstracts).

title: Sharp singularity rates for symmetric random sign matrices
problem: The singularity probability of a symmetric sign matrix is (1/2+o(1))^n for uniform signs and (p²+(1−p)²+o(1))^n for bias p≠1/2.
method: The extremal event is that two rows agree, so the exponential rate is the probability of that coincidence.

title: Shelah's eventual categoricity and the prescribed-threshold obstruction
problem: Shelah's eventual categoricity holds in ZFC, and under the continuum hypothesis a proposed specific Hanf threshold does not suffice.
method: Under CH, builds an abstract elementary class with Löwenheim–Skolem number ℵ0 that is categorical in all large cardinals but has two nonisomorphic models at beth_{ω2}; the abstract gives no further method.

title: Rigidity of the Turing degrees
problem: Every order automorphism of the Turing degrees is the identity.

title: Single-fold Diophantine representations and undecidability under an at-most-one-solution promise
problem: Every recursively enumerable set of tuples has a Diophantine representation with exactly one auxiliary solution per member, and solvability with an at-most-one promise stays undecidable.

title: Separating choiceless counting from polynomial time and witnessed choice
problem: Choiceless polynomial time with counting does not capture polynomial time, and witnessed symmetric choice strictly increases its expressive power.
method: Separation by a polynomial-time query defined by consistency of a linear system over F_3, which the counting formalism cannot express.

title: The Partition Principle does not imply Choice
problem: Assuming ZF is consistent, the Partition Principle and Choice for ordinal-indexed families do not imply the full Axiom of Choice.
method: Transitive symmetric extension of a countable transitive ZFC model that adds no new countable sequences of ground-model elements.

title: Weak and strong normalization in pure type systems
problem: Every weakly beta-normalizing pure type system is strongly beta-normalizing, with no functionality hypothesis.

title: Cannon's conjecture
problem: Every hyperbolic group with boundary homeomorphic to the 2-sphere acts properly and cocompactly isometrically on hyperbolic 3-space with finite kernel.
method: Modulus-based argument (named in the paper title; the abstract gives no details).

title: An infinite finitely presented residually finite 2-group and a finitely presented nil algebra
problem: Constructs an infinite finitely presented residually finite group in which every element has 2-power order, and a finitely presented infinite-dimensional nil algebra over F_2.
method: Finite-index subgroup of a Steinberg group St_12(R), with residual finiteness shown by finite-degree truncations that detect elements through phases of long words in a graded algebra.

title: Thompson's group F is nonamenable
problem: Thompson's group F, the dyadic piecewise linear homeomorphisms of the interval, is nonamenable.

title: A finitely generated Eilenberg-Ganea counterexample
problem: Constructs a finitely generated residually finite group with integral cohomological dimension 2 and geometric dimension 3.

title: Boone-Higman embeddings with higher finiteness
problem: A finitely generated group has decidable word problem exactly when it embeds in a finitely presented simple group, and the target can be of type F_infinity.
method: Finite algebraic envelopes (named in the paper titles; the abstract gives no argument).

title: Amenability, unitarizability, and strong Ulam stability
problem: A discrete group is amenable if and only if its uniformly bounded representations are all unitarizable, and, for countable groups, if and only if it is strongly Ulam stable.

title: A torsion-free hyperbolic group that is neither residually finite nor linear over any field
problem: Constructs a torsion-free word-hyperbolic group that is not residually finite and has a nonidentity element killed by every finite-dimensional linear representation over every field.

title: An infinite finitely presented simple amenable group
problem: Constructs an infinite finitely presented simple amenable group.

title: Classifying spaces and geometric obstructions for Artin groups
problem: The Salvetti complex of every finite-rank Artin group is aspherical, parabolic subgroups are closed under intersection, and one explicit Artin group has no geometric CAT(0) action.
method: Harmonic heights of the Salvetti complex (named in the paper title; the abstract gives no argument).

title: Quasi-isometric recognition of virtually polycyclic groups
problem: Every finitely generated group quasi-isometric to a finitely generated virtually polycyclic group is virtually polycyclic.

title: Nonsingular systems of equations over arbitrary groups
problem: Every finite nonsingular system of equations over a group has a simultaneous solution in an overgroup, and one generator and one relation cannot trivialize a nontrivial group.

title: A hyperbolic group without a geometric CAT(0) action
problem: Constructs a hyperbolic group with a finite classifying space that admits no proper cocompact isometric action on a proper complete CAT(0) space.

title: Gersten's conjecture and virtual compact specialness of one-relator groups
problem: Every one-relator group with no Baumslag-Solitar subgroup is word-hyperbolic, and every word-hyperbolic one-relator group is virtually compact special.

title: A group without fixed price
problem: Constructs a finitely generated group with two essentially free measure-preserving actions of different costs, answering Gaboriau's general fixed-price problem negatively.
method: Amalgam of a free group of rank 100 with a direct product, comparing the cost of a Bernoulli action (bounded away from one) with the costs of finite height extensions (tending to one).

title: Spacetime Penrose inequalities: enclosing area, charge, rotation, and anti-de Sitter extensions
problem: Proves the sharp enclosing-area spacetime Penrose inequality for one-ended asymptotically flat data in every spatial dimension n >= 3, with charged and anti-de Sitter variants.
method: Reduction of the purely electric higher-dimensional case to the matched neutral theorem, with equality rigidity under horizon hypotheses.

title: Localization and delocalization in the Anderson model
problem: The two-dimensional Anderson model has pure-point spectrum at every positive disorder, and weak disorder in dimension at least three gives absolutely continuous spectrum on an open interval.

title: Sharp finite-matrix Lieb-Thirring inequalities and all equality cases
problem: For 1/2 < gamma < 3/2 the sharp one-dimensional Lieb-Thirring constant for matrix potentials equals the scalar one-bound-state constant, and equality holds only for direct sums of scalar sech^2 solitons.

title: The ionization and generalized ionization conjectures
problem: Molecules with M fixed nuclei bind at most Z+CM electrons, and neutral-atom ionization energies and radii have universal bounds and Thomas-Fermi asymptotics.

title: Strong cosmic censorship near two-ended Kerr data
problem: Generic vacuum data near a two-ended rotating subextremal Kerr bridge have no future continuous extension with locally square-integrable weak connection, and analogous C^1 and C^2 statements hold.
method: Baire category argument: dense G-delta and meagre sets in a weighted smooth topology.

title: Area laws and tensor networks for two-dimensional gapped systems
problem: Proves an entropy area law for unique ground states of finite-range Hamiltonians on arbitrary finite square-lattice domains, and polynomial-bond-dimension PEPS approximations on L x L squares with error L^-1.
method: Area law from a global spectral gap alone, bounding entanglement entropy by the number of boundary edges, plus an existence proof for PEPS approximations.

title: The maximum number of mutually unbiased bases in dimension six
problem: The maximum number of mutually unbiased bases in C^6 is three, resolving Zauner's conjecture.
method: Certified binary64 computation excluding four bases, together with an exact integer and rational Fourier-vanishing certificate excluding seven bases (companion paper).

title: Positive-temperature Bose-Einstein condensation and exact quantum depletion
problem: Bose-Einstein condensation at positive temperature in the dilute hard-sphere gas, and the Bogoliubov quantum-depletion law at zero temperature.
method: unclear from abstract (the thermodynamic limit is taken before the dilute limit).

title: The spin-one Haldane gap
problem: Uniform positive spectral gap for the pure antiferromagnetic spin-one Heisenberg chain on even periodic rings, and a gap for odd open chains with boundary field 3/5.
method: Explicit gap bound log(10)/392 for odd open chains with L >= 960 (companion), with Tasaki's index theorem giving index -1 for the boundary-selected local limits.

title: Uniform Laughlin gap and stability under bounded scalar disorder
problem: The fermionic Laughlin state at filling 1/3 on the round sphere has a uniform gap for the V1 interaction and stays gapped under weak bounded lowest-Landau-level potentials.
method: Operator inequality H_Q^2 >= gamma H_Q on the lowest-Landau-level Fock space with gamma > 1/25, uniform in flux (companion paper), with perturbation stability from the uniform unperturbed gap.

title: Threshold and positive-energy bound states of the BFSS matrix model
problem: The undeformed relative SU(N) BFSS model has exactly one normalizable zero-energy state for each N >= 2, and the SU(2) model has infinitely many normalizable positive-energy eigenstates.
method: Positive-energy operator defined by closing the gauge-invariant supercharge form (companion abstract); the zero-energy count is not described.

title: Bloch's law, its lattice correction, and the spherical magnetization law
problem: Proves Bloch's T^{3/2} law with its exact coefficient for three-dimensional quantum Heisenberg ferromagnets, plus the first lattice correction and spontaneous magnetization.
method: The leading coefficient is fixed by the determinant of the quadratic one-magnon dispersion, computed through the ideal magnon density.

title: Entanglement with zero distillable secret key in local dimension ten
problem: Constructs an entangled state on C^10 tensor C^10 with zero distillable secret key for specified local-instrument protocols, and a trace-preserving PPT channel on M_21(C) whose square is not entanglement breaking.
method: The state is the normalized Choi matrix of a composition of two PPT maps built from an integer 6-by-4 matrix pencil, and a coherence inequality on key branches gives a uniform trace-distance gap of 1/5 for the operational protocols.
location: pp. 2-4 (Section 1 overview; operational obstruction and dimension-ten construction on pp. 3-4)

title: The entropy photon-number inequality
problem: Proves the entropy photon-number inequality for beam-splitter mixing of two finite-energy bosonic inputs in any finite number of modes, with equality for product thermal inputs.

title: Parity is not in QAC0
problem: Constant-depth circuits with one-qubit gates and unbounded-arity Toffoli gates cannot compute parity with any fixed positive worst-case advantage using polynomially many qubits in the measured-output model.
method: Product-projection localization and pruning of regular trajectories (named in the paper titles; the abstract gives no argument).

title: QMA-hardness of continuum Coulomb energy
problem: Approximating the electronic Coulomb ground-energy infimum in three dimensions is QMA-hard, even with unit nuclear charges at distinct rational positions.
method: Deterministic polynomial-time classical reduction from QMA verification to the Coulomb spectral infimum, with threshold separation at least one.

title: Classical capacity of generalized amplitude damping
problem: Determines the unassisted classical capacity of every qubit generalized amplitude-damping channel and proves additivity under tensor products with finite-dimensional channels.
method: Reduction of the capacity to a one-variable maximum attained by binary pure-state ensembles, plus additivity of Holevo capacity and minimum output entropy under tensoring.

title: Threshold repetition for entangled games
problem: For a two-player game with entangled value v < 1, the probability of winning at least a fraction v + delta of k repetitions decays exponentially in k.

title: Failure of Kohn-Sham ensemble representation
problem: Constructs a three-electron Coulomb molecule whose ground-state density has no noninteracting ground-state ensemble representation by a single local potential in L^{3/2} + L^infinity.
method: unclear from abstract (the nuclear charges are fixed by an explicit nonnumerical formula).

title: Exact quantum factoring over a fixed finite gate set
problem: A polynomial-time uniform quantum circuit family outputs the complete prime factorization of every integer with probability one, over one fixed finite gate set.

title: Unitary vertex operator algebras and conformal nets
problem: Every simple unitary strongly rational vertex operator algebra generates a completely rational conformal net, with matching braided representation categories.
method: Carpi-Weiner-Xu functor from grading-restricted modules to finite-index sectors, shown to be a braided unitary tensor equivalence, combined with Gui's extension theorems.

title: QAOA attains the SK ground-state energy in the thermodynamic-first limit
problem: QAOA with fixed finite-depth angles approaches the ground-state energy per spin of the Gaussian zero-field Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model as system size grows before depth.
method: Infinite-size limit taken first, with depth-p angles chosen independent of system size and disorder; the abstract gives no quantitative depth bound.

title: From scale symmetry to local conformal symmetry in four-dimensional QFT
problem: Scale symmetry implies local conformal Ward identities for four-dimensional unitary positive-energy theories with discrete bounded-below scaling spectrum.

title: Polynomial-time unitary synthesis from a Boolean oracle
problem: A uniform polynomial-size quantum oracle circuit approximates every n-qubit unitary to full diamond-norm error 1/2, using a target-dependent Boolean oracle.
method: Recursive reduction of a d-dimensional unitary to one smaller controlled unitary via a block-matrix transfer-function identity after random diagonal signs and Walsh transforms, with Fourier-multiset encodings of sparse maps and amplitude amplification.
location: pp. 2-4 (Sections 1.3 and 2; the recursion and resource bounds in Sections 4-6 were not read)

title: The optimal quartic separation between randomized and quantum queries
problem: Total Boolean functions with nearly quartic separation between randomized and quantum query complexity, so that R(f) = O((1+Q(f))^4) is optimal in its exponent.
method: Addressed certificates with outward pointers across m columns, a tournament lemma giving a short list that contains the winner, and a k-fold Forrelation partial function whose query bound follows from a direct-product argument.
location: pp. 2-4 (Sections 1.2 and 2.1, Lemma 2.1; Section 3 tournament lemma not read)

title: Counterexamples to Baum-Connes and Kadison-Kaplansky
problem: Disproves the coefficient-free reduced Baum-Connes conjecture through failures of rational injectivity and of surjectivity of assembly, and disproves the Kadison-Kaplansky projection conjecture.

title: Rigidity and arithmetic of lattice von Neumann algebras
problem: Classifies finite-index bimodules between scalar-twisted group factors of ICC groups commensurable with property (T) lattices and arbitrary ICC group factors.
method: Every such bimodule is a summand of a finite sum of models built from finite-index subgroup isomorphisms and finite-dimensional projective representations.

title: Isomorphism of the free group factors
problem: L(F_2) is isomorphic to L(F_3), so all interpolated free group factors, including L(F_infinity), are isomorphic with fundamental group R_{>0}.

title: Kadison's similarity conjecture
problem: Every bounded unital homomorphism from a unital C*-algebra into bounded operators on a Hilbert space is similar to a *-homomorphism.
method: Similarity obtained through uniform derivation estimates (named in the preprint title; the abstract gives no further step).

title: Strong Kadison–Kastler stability and its spatial boundaries
problem: Sufficiently close unital von Neumann algebras are conjugate by a unitary near the identity, with a universal tolerance; one-sided near inclusions and close separable C*-algebras show sharp failures.

title: Relative bicentralizers and modular spectral recovery
problem: Connes' bicentralizer conjecture holds for type III1 factors with separable predual, and the relative version holds for inclusions with a faithful normal conditional expectation.
method: Construct an amenable expected subalgebra P of N whose commutant intersected with the continuous core c(M) equals that of N.

title: Cuntz comparison, nuclear dimension, and equivariant Jiang–Su stability
problem: Equivariant Jiang–Su stability holds for amenable group actions on simple nuclear algebras, and strict comparison, finite nuclear dimension and Jiang–Su stability are equivalent in the unital case.

title: Kirchberg's O_2 norm-ultrapower embedding problem
problem: A separable unital full group C*-algebra admits no unital embedding into the norm ultrapower of any nonzero unital nuclear algebra, including O_2.
method: Explicit algebra-level obstruction to unital embedding into norm ultrapowers (named in the preprint title; the abstract does not describe it).

title: Invariant projections, hyperinvariant subspaces, and transitive algebras
problem: A nonzero norm-quasinilpotent operator on every infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space has no nonzero proper hyperinvariant subspace, and some such operators have no nontrivial invariant projection in the hyperfinite II1 factor.
method: Weighted irrational rotation: a continuous nonnegative circle weight with exactly one zero and logarithmic integral minus infinity, giving a weighted rotation with no invariant projection.

title: Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture and failure of tensor-product stable finiteness
problem: A separable unital C*-algebra has normalized 2-quasitraces but no tracial state, which refutes Kaplansky's conjecture and yields a properly infinite minimal tensor product of stably finite algebras.
method: Construct an algebra that admits normalized 2-quasitraces, all nonadditive, and no tracial state.

title: The Kadison–Ringrose cohomology conjecture
problem: Every bounded Hochschild cocycle of degree at least two on a complex von Neumann algebra has a bounded primitive, so higher bounded Hochschild cohomology vanishes.

title: The generator problem for finite factors
problem: Every type II1 factor with separable predual is generated by one operator, equivalently by two self-adjoint operators.
method: Single-factor generation argument, combined with an established direct-integral reduction to type II1 factors (the abstract gives no further detail of the new step).

title: A ZFC counterexample to Naimark's problem
problem: A unital infinite-dimensional simple C*-algebra with a faithful tracial state has all nonzero irreducible representations unitarily equivalent, in ZFC; the example is nonseparable.

title: Two notions of free entropy differ even when both are finite
problem: A bounded self-adjoint tuple has microstates free entropy at most nonmicrostates free entropy minus one half, with both values finite.
method: Explicit bounded self-adjoint tuple with a large but fixed number of variables, separated by an entropy gap of at least one half.

title: The Kirchberg–Rørdam character criterion and infinite tensor-power Jiang–Su stability
problem: A unital separable C*-algebra absorbs the Jiang–Su algebra exactly when its norm central-sequence algebra has no characters, and its infinite minimal tensor powers are Z-stable.
method: Characterize Z-stability by the absence of characters on the norm central-sequence algebra, for every free ultrafilter.

title: Approximation and quadratic strong-operator paving
problem: Every self-adjoint element of a von Neumann algebra admits strong-operator paving over any maximal abelian subalgebra with O(ε^-2) projections (quadratic paving conjecture of Popa and Vaes).
method: Approximate by self-adjoints of at most three times the norm, pave each approximant with error relative to its own norm, then compress by a projection near the identity in the strong topology.

title: Trace cones and Razak–Jacelon stabilization
problem: The cone of extended lower-semicontinuous tracial weights classifies separable nuclear C*-algebras after tensoring with the Razak–Jacelon algebra and the compact operators.
method: Use the full topological cone of tracial weights as a complete invariant after Razak–Jacelon stabilization.

title: Radius of comparison equals half the mean dimension
problem: For a minimal homeomorphism of an infinite compact metrizable space, the radius of comparison of the crossed product equals half the mean dimension, including infinite values.

title: Weak pure infiniteness and Cuntz-algebra absorption
problem: Every C*-algebra in which each positive element is properly infinite is strongly purely infinite; for exact algebras, one fixed finite amplification suffices, and separable nuclear algebras absorb O_infinity.
method: Reduce strong pure infiniteness to proper infiniteness of positive elements, with a fixed finite amplification sufficing for exact algebras.

title: The Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every dimension
problem: Every locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group acting faithfully and jointly continuously on a connected finite-dimensional manifold is a Lie group.

title: Four-dimensional disk embedding and Wall's conjecture
problem: The unrestricted disk-embedding conjecture fails, the free group on two generators is not good, and a finitely presented PD4 group with a finite classifying space is not realized by a closed aspherical 4-manifold.
method: Construct immersed disks with framed algebraic dual spheres in a compact smooth 4-manifold that admit no disjoint locally flat boundary-preserving replacements, and a PD4 group with no aspherical manifold model.

title: The purely cosmetic surgery conjecture
problem: Distinct Dehn surgery slopes on a nontrivial smooth knot in S^3 never give orientation-preservingly homeomorphic manifolds, including the meridional slope.

title: Failure of rational injectivity for maximal coarse assembly
problem: A uniformly discrete bounded-geometry space has an infinite-order class in the kernel of maximal coarse assembly, which disproves the rational coarse Novikov conjecture.
method: Coarse disjoint union of finite connected graphs of bounded degree, with an infinite-order class in degree-one coarse K-homology that maps to zero under coarse assembly.

title: Finite Smith–Toda complexes at every height
problem: For each height n there is a finite p-local spectrum with Brown–Peterson homology BP_*/(p, v_1, ..., v_n), with the prime depending on n; V(4) is realized at p = 1009.

title: The Kervaire invariant problem at the prime three
problem: Exactly the standard Kervaire classes at indices 0, 2 and 3 survive in the mod-3 Adams spectral sequence, in stems 10, 106 and 322.

title: Quillen's conjecture in rational homology
problem: For a finite group with trivial largest normal p-subgroup, the poset of nontrivial elementary abelian p-subgroups has nonzero augmented reduced rational homology.

title: The Hovey–Strickland and Chai conjectures
problem: Dualizable K(n)-local spectra have exactly n+2 thick tensor ideals, and their Balmer spectrum is a chain of n+1 points.
method: Classify the prime and radical ideals of the Lubin–Tate deformation ring that are invariant under an open Morava stabilizer subgroup.

title: The Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis
problem: Weak globular infinity-groupoids from every Grothendieck coherator in the Ara–Henry convention recover the homotopy theory of spaces.
method: Elementary expansions, shown to preserve components and all homotopy groups of cellular infinity-groupoids (this also resolves Henry's pushout conjecture).

title: Finite generation for the K(n)-local sphere
problem: Every homotopy group of the K(n)-local sphere is a finitely generated Z_p-module, for every prime, positive height and integer degree.

title: Cyclic length and chromatic fixed-point loss
problem: The optimal chromatic loss from geometric H-fixed points to geometric G-fixed points equals the shortest subnormal chain from H to G with cyclic quotients.
method: Identify the loss with a combinatorial chain length in which each cyclic quotient counts once regardless of its order; finite spectra witness sharpness.

title: The four-dimensional Singer conjecture
problem: L2-Betti numbers of the universal cover of a closed aspherical topological 4-manifold vanish outside degree two, and the same holds for finite aspherical integral Poincaré complexes of formal dimension four.

title: Curtis's conjecture
problem: The positive-degree mod-two stable Hurewicz image of the sphere is spanned by η, ν, σ and the Kervaire-invariant-one classes that exist.

title: Thomason model structures in all strict higher dimensions
problem: Small strict globular n-categories admit proper combinatorial model structures Quillen equivalent to simplicial sets, for every n from 1 to infinity and for dimension omega.
method: Model structure with weak equivalences and fibrations detected by the twice-extended Street nerve Ex^2 N_n, with Quillen equivalence c_n Sd^2 left adjoint to Ex^2 N_n.

title: Chromatic splitting: filtrations and counterexamples
problem: Strong chromatic splitting fails at height three for p at least 5, weak splitting fails at heights p and p+1, and the overlap has a 2^n-stage filtration by localized-sphere pieces when p is greater than n+1.
method: Filtration of the chromatic overlap by the predicted localized-sphere pieces (the headline gives no construction detail).

title: Counterexamples to finite generation at chromatic height two
problem: For every sufficiently large prime p there is a connective p-complete spectrum of exact fp-type two outside the thick subcategory generated by BP<2>.

title: Nonhomeomorphic closed aspherical four-manifolds
problem: Closed aspherical topological 4-manifolds that are homotopy equivalent but not homeomorphic exist, with a common word-hyperbolic fundamental group.

title: A counterexample to Wall's finite D(2) problem
problem: A finite connected 3-dimensional CW complex satisfies D(2) but is not homotopy equivalent to any finite 2-dimensional complex; its fundamental group is infinite.

title: Tingley's sphere-isometry problem
problem: Every surjective isometry between unit spheres of real Banach spaces extends uniquely to a surjective real-linear isometry of the whole spaces.
method: Extension argument using common supports and Darbo's fixed-point theorem to align extremal chords, with a contradiction from support and convexity estimates (named in the preprint abstract).

title: Independence of the separable quotient problem
problem: The separable quotient problem is independent of ZFC relative to a measurable cardinal, over both the real and complex fields.

title: Lipschitz equivalent Banach spaces need not be linearly isomorphic
problem: There are separable real Banach spaces that are globally bi-Lipschitz equivalent but not linearly isomorphic.

title: The complete Crouzeix conjecture
problem: For a bounded operator A and a matrix-valued polynomial P, the norm of P[A] is at most 2 times the supremum of the norm of P over the numerical range W(A), with constant 2 sharp.
method: Direct proof of the matrix inequality (named in a preprint title); a second preprint represents evaluation through one positive boundary density and an optimal similarity with condition number at most two.

title: The cotype–cotype conjecture under the approximation property
problem: A nonzero real Banach space with the approximation property is K-convex if and only if it and its dual have finite Rademacher cotype.

title: Markov type characterizes superreflexivity
problem: Every real Banach space with Markov type p for some p greater than 1 is superreflexive, which characterizes superreflexivity by nontrivial Markov type.

title: Nonexpansive fixed points in reflexive Banach spaces
problem: Every nonexpansive self-map of a nonempty closed bounded convex subset of a real reflexive Banach space has a fixed point, in the original norm.

title: A counterexample to metric-entropy duality
problem: Pietsch's dimension-free duality between covering numbers and polar bodies fails for origin-symmetric convex bodies, already when the covering body is a cube.
method: Construction of origin-symmetric convex bodies that violate the covering-entropy inequality for every choice of constants (the abstract does not describe the construction).

title: A uniformly discrete counterexample to bounded approximation in Lipschitz-free spaces
problem: A countable uniformly discrete metric space has a real Lipschitz-free space with the approximation property but not the bounded approximation property.

title: Reflexive midpoint convexity and diamond distortion
problem: A reflexive real Banach space is asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex but has no equivalent asymptotically uniformly convex norm, and the depth-k countably branching diamond has distortion at least sqrt(1+k/12).
method: Explicit tree-space construction with a midpoint-modulus estimate, which gives the distortion lower bound for the countably branching diamond.

title: Metric Markov cotype of ℓ1 and Hilbert-space Lipschitz extension
problem: Real ℓ1 has metric Markov cotype two, so Lipschitz maps from subsets of a Hilbert space into ℓ1 extend with a universal multiplicative loss.

title: Smooth isometric immersions of surfaces into ℝ4
problem: Every closed smooth Riemannian surface, orientable or not, admits a smooth isometric immersion into Euclidean four-space.

title: A smooth surface metric with no local isometric immersion in ℝ3
problem: A smooth positive-definite metric on (-1,1)^2 that is flat to all orders at the origin has no neighborhood admitting a smooth isometric immersion into Euclidean three-space.

title: Gromov's integral scalar-curvature bound for simplicial volume.
problem: Shows the integral of (negative part of scalar curvature)^(n/2) is at least a_n times real simplicial volume, and that positive scalar curvature forces rational inessentiality.
method: Deduces the integral bound from a nonnegative-scalar-curvature vanishing theorem proved in a companion paper.

title: Spectral scalar curvature, Urysohn width, and macroscopic dimension.
problem: Maps complete manifolds with spectral scalar curvature at least 1 continuously to a complex of dimension n-2 with fibers of bounded diameter.

title: Sharp Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetry and rigidity.
problem: Proves sharp isoperimetric and filling inequalities in nonpositively curved spaces, with Euclidean balls as the equality case.

title: Yau's uniformization conjecture.
problem: Shows every complete noncompact Kähler manifold with positive holomorphic bisectional curvature is biholomorphic to C^n.

title: Katok's entropy rigidity conjecture.
problem: Shows Liouville measure maximizes geodesic-flow entropy exactly when a closed negatively curved manifold of dimension at least three is locally symmetric.

title: A counterexample to the nearby Lagrangian conjecture.
problem: Constructs a closed exact Lagrangian in T*(S^9 x S^(N-1)) that is diffeomorphic to the base but not Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section.

title: Donaldson's hypersymplectic deformation conjecture.
problem: Shows every normalized positive closed triple of two-forms on a closed oriented four-manifold deforms, with fixed cohomology, to a hyperkähler triple.

title: Donaldson's tamed-to-compatible conjecture.
problem: Shows every almost complex structure on a closed four-manifold tamed by a symplectic form is compatible with some symplectic form.

title: Symplectic ball packing in higher dimensions.
problem: Determines exactly when finitely many balls of arbitrary capacities embed disjointly into a ball in dimensions 2n >= 6 (Siegel–Yao conjecture).

title: The metric Blaschke conjecture.
problem: Shows a closed Riemannian manifold whose injectivity radius equals its diameter is, up to scale, a standard rank-one symmetric space.

title: Infinitely many closed geodesics on Riemannian spheres and closed three-manifolds.
problem: Shows every Riemannian sphere and every closed three-manifold carries infinitely many prime closed geodesics with pairwise distinct images.
method: Extends the sphere result to closed three-manifolds using finite covers and theorems of Perelman and Rademacher–Taimanov; the sphere-case method is not stated.

title: Sharp singular-set bounds for stationary integral varifolds.
problem: Shows the singular set of a stationary integral m-varifold in Euclidean space has Hausdorff dimension at most m-1, and is null on round spheres.

title: Counterexamples to stable-Morse and strong Arnold fixed-point bounds.
problem: Gives Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms with fewer nondegenerate fixed points than the stable Morse number, and a quadric threefold map with three fixed points.
method: Builds a Kähler example from a Hamiltonian involution with integral homology torsion at two primes, and counts fixed points with finite-dimensional Morse theory and complex blowups (companion abstract).

title: Nonnegative-curvature Einstein classification and an L^2 topological gap.
problem: Classifies positive-Einstein nonnegatively curved closed four-manifolds, and identifies simply connected ones by a small L^2 norm of trace-free Ricci curvature.
method: Extends coupled estimates on the two Weyl curvature blocks to the boundary of the sectional-curvature cone to fix the equality case; the L^2 gap takes that classification as a premise.

title: The Solomon–Yau least-volume conjecture.
problem: Shows every closed minimal immersion with non-totally-geodesic image into the unit sphere has volume at least that of the smallest minimal Clifford product.

title: Yau's nodal bounds: surfaces and higher dimensions.
problem: Proves the sharp C sqrt(lambda) nodal length bound on smooth surfaces and shows the upper bound fails in dimensions three and four.

title: Scalar curvature and finite-time Ricci-flow singularities.
problem: Shows bounded scalar curvature rules out finite-time singularities of Ricci flow on closed four-manifolds, and higher-dimensional examples have bounded scalar curvature with unbounded curvature.

title: A finite-time singularity of Calabi flow.
problem: Constructs a U(10)-invariant Kähler metric in the Fubini–Study class of CP^10 whose Calabi flow blows up in finite time.

title: Affine Bernstein rigidity through dimension nine and a smooth dimension-ten counterexample.
problem: Proves elliptic-paraboloid rigidity for complete affine maximal graphs in dimensions three to nine and gives a smooth nonquadratic entire example in dimension ten.

title: The isoperimetric profile of the cubic three-torus.
problem: Determines the isoperimetric profile of the unit cubic flat three-torus and classifies all minimizers.

title: Unique tangent flows at the first surface singularity.
problem: Shows that at the first singular time of embedded surface mean curvature flow in R^3, all fixed-center backward tangent flows agree at each singular point.

title: Gigli’s characterization of Alexandrov curvature.
problem: Shows Alexandrov curvature at least kappa is equivalent to a full-support RCD((n-1)kappa, n) condition plus distributional sectional curvature bounds, in every dimension n >= 2.

title: Bi-Lipschitz coordinates at every regular RCD point.
problem: Shows every regular point of a noncollapsed RCD(K,n) space has a neighborhood bi-Lipschitz to an open subset of R^n.

title: A three-manifold without conjugate points or nonpositive curvature.
problem: Constructs a closed orientable three-manifold with a metric without conjugate points but no metric of nonpositive sectional curvature.

title: Negative Kähler curvature without bounded holomorphic coordinates.
problem: Constructs a contractible domain in C^3 with a complete negatively pinched Kähler metric and no bounded holomorphic coordinates.

title: Weak MTW curvature gives convexity and regular optimal transport.
problem: Shows weak MTW curvature makes every tangent injectivity domain convex and gives Hölder regularity of optimal maps between densities bounded above and below.
method: Establishes that every subgradient of the squared-distance cost potential is a minimizing velocity with a global supporting mountain.

title: Failure of integer-degree harmonic dimension comparison.
problem: Constructs complete metrics on R^n with nonnegative Ricci curvature that have more independent harmonic functions of integer growth k than the Euclidean count.

title: Global smoothness for relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell.
problem: Proves global existence and uniqueness of smooth solutions for arbitrary smooth data in the 3D one-species relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system.

title: Nonuniqueness with local conservation for the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation.
problem: Constructs two distinct global entropy solutions from one initial density for the periodic hard-sphere Boltzmann equation, both locally conserving mass, momentum and energy.

title: Kinetic limits and fluctuations over the Boltzmann lifespan.
problem: Derives the nonlinear Boltzmann equation from grand-canonical Newtonian gases and proves a Gaussian fluctuation limit for hard spheres on the same time intervals.

title: Joint metric and connection recovery from one boundary patch.
problem: Shows zero-frequency boundary data on one open patch determine a metric and unitary connection up to diffeomorphism and gauge.

title: The planar Mumford–Shah regularity conjecture and local weak-L^4 gradient bounds.
field: Free discontinuity problems, calculus of variations
problem: Shows the discontinuity set of a reduced planar Mumford–Shah minimizer is locally a C^(1,alpha) arc, a crack tip, or three arcs meeting at 120 degrees.

title: The critical dimension for the one-phase Bernoulli problem.
problem: Shows dimension seven is the first with a nonflat one-homogeneous global minimizer, so minimizing free boundaries are smooth through dimension six.

title: The three-dimensional Ball–Evans approximation problem.
problem: Shows every W^(1,p) homeomorphism between bounded domains in R^3 is a strong W^(1,p) limit of smooth diffeomorphisms, for 1 <= p < infinity.

title: The hot spots conjecture for simply connected planar domains.
problem: Shows every nonzero first Neumann eigenfunction on a smooth simply connected planar domain has no interior critical point, so its extrema lie on the boundary.

title: The Lane–Emden and Hénon–Lane–Emden conjectures.
problem: Shows the weighted Lane–Emden system has no positive entire solution under a sharp exponent inequality, with no symmetry or growth assumption.

title: Stable blowup for the defocusing Schrödinger equation.
problem: Shows that for a sufficiently large odd power, an open set of H^k(T^12) initial data blows up in finite time for the defocusing NLS.
method: Builds self-similar blowup profiles and shows finite-time blowup persists under open perturbations of the initial data in a high Sobolev space.

title: Global uniqueness in smooth isotropic elasticity.
problem: Shows full static displacement-to-traction data determine both smooth Lamé moduli on bounded smooth domains in R^3 under mu > 0 and 3λ+2μ > 0.

title: Nonattainment of the three-marginal Coulomb Monge problem.
problem: Shows the three-marginal Coulomb Monge infimum equals the Kantorovich infimum but is not attained for a smooth density, and the same holds for inverse-power costs.

title: Sharp one-third stability of Brenier maps.
problem: Shows quadratic optimal maps to the uniform density on a convex body are one-third Hölder stable in L^2 with respect to W2, and the exponent is sharp.

title: De Giorgi's conjecture in dimension eight.
problem: Shows entire solutions of Δu = u^3 - u on R^8 that are monotone in one direction depend on one coordinate, and classifies stable solutions on R^7.

title: Universal computation in forced Navier–Stokes flows.
problem: Shows smooth forces on a fixed flat three-dimensional domain can make a fluid particle reach a fixed region exactly when a Turing machine halts.
method: A terminating compiler turns a Turing machine and input into a finite forcing program, using reciprocal affine instruction maps realized by incompressible shear flows.

title: Interior C^(1,alpha) regularity for infinity-harmonic functions.
problem: Shows bounded infinity-harmonic functions in dimension d >= 3 are C^(1,alpha_d) with a uniform interior estimate in terms of oscillation.

title: Disproof of the Exponential Time Hypothesis.
problem: Gives a deterministic algorithm that counts satisfying assignments of any fixed-k CNF in time (n+m)^(O_k(1)) 2^(n/(log n)^(1/2+o(1))), which refutes ETH.
method: Reduces to bounded-occurrence k-CNF, writes the count as a polynomial sum, replaces clause inputs by low-degree linear forms so variable groups interact only through a few shared linear summaries, then counts each group and recovers the total by interpolation.

title: Euclidean tensor geometry and its applications to complexity and combinatorics.
problem: Gives matrix multiplication exponent 9/4 over every field, circuit lower bounds for Hamiltonian cycle and the permanent, and an exponential bound for sunflower-free families.
method: Assigns each tensor a log-invariant cost, so that a bit shared by several sites costs the mean width of their convex hull, and compares tensor prices with network sizes using additivity, multiplicativity and monotonicity under linear maps.
location: Section 1 and Theorem 1.1 (pp. 1-3); sunflower step in companion paper, not read

title: Strongly polynomial-time linear programming.
problem: Gives a deterministic strongly polynomial algorithm for real linear programs and disproves the polynomial Hirsch conjecture with superpolynomial graph diameter.

title: Saturated triangle incidence in hypothetical (5,5,45) graphs
field: Ramsey theory, local counting in (4,5,m) neighbourhoods
problem: Proves that a hypothetical (5,5,45) graph has at least 455 saturated monochromatic triangles, and that if each colored edge lies in at most two of them the graph is 22-regular with 110 edges in each colored neighbourhood.
method: Profile-count linear programme for (4,5,m) neighbourhoods, using the identities of [3, Thm 2.2] and an auxiliary graph Q(H) of edges with four common neighbours, with the edge bound certified by exact rational dual vectors.
checked: partial: exact rational dual vectors checked by a standard-library Python verifier (per paper, supplement not opened); catalogue completeness imported

title: Local structure of a hypothetical (5,5)-good conference graph on 45 vertices
field: Ramsey theory, strongly regular graphs, SAT calibration
problem: For every edge of an srg(45,22,10,11) the common neighbourhood H satisfies 12(e(H)-15) equal to a sum of terms nonnegative at integers, so every edge lies in at least 15 copies of K4; every vertex of a (5,5)-good conference graph lies on an edge in at least three saturated triangles.
method: A per-edge codegree identity whose squared-deviation terms are nonnegative at integers, combined with 16 rooted SAT refutations of the 22-vertex local graph whose proofs are DRAT-checked.

title: Exclusion of Prime Automorphisms of Order p >= 7 on (5,5,42)- and (5,5,43)-Graphs
problem: No (5,5,42) or (5,5,43) graph has an automorphism of prime order 7 or higher, so |Aut| has only the prime factors 2, 3 and 5 for those graphs at those orders.
method: Fixed-vertex deletion from 43 to 42 vertices, analytic exclusion of fixed-point counts using R(3,3)=6 and R(4,5)=25, and two independent exhaustive C++ censuses of 7^6 polycirculants that report no solutions.
checked: partial: two C++ exhaustive censuses (canonical solver and standalone verifier), each reporting 0 solutions; no proof certificate named

title: Exclusion of Prime Automorphisms p >= 5 and Solvability of Aut(G) on (5,5,42)-, (5,5,43)-, and (5,5,44)-Graphs
field: Ramsey theory, graph automorphisms, monotone SAT surgery
problem: Excludes all prime orders p >= 7 on 42 to 45 vertices and order 5 on 42 to 44 vertices, so Aut is solvable of order 2^a 3^b for 42 to 44 vertices; fixed-point-free order 5 at 45 vertices stays open.
method: Fixed-vertex deletion to fixed-point-free 11^4 polycirculants, dual independent C++ censuses with 0 solutions, and an exact global monotone SAT solver whose unit-locking of red edges is UNSAT across 2,860 seeds.
checked: partial: two independent C++ census solvers (0 solutions each) and an exact SAT/DPLL surgery solver; no DRAT or LRAT proof named

title: Automorphisms of window R-graphs and of a (5,5)-good conference graph on 45 vertices
field: Ramsey theory, strongly regular graphs, orbit matrices
problem: Every prime dividing Aut of an R-graph is 2 or 11, the window excludes the order-11 and order-4 R-graphs, and Aut of a (5,5)-good srg(45,22,10,11) is an elementary abelian 2-group fixing a vertex.
method: Exact window test on candidate local graphs, SAT encodings of cycle types of orders 3, 5, 7 and 4 (kissat, DRAT-checked by drat-trim, with a CP-SAT cross-check), and an orbit-matrix system B^2 = 45I - 5J that rules out fixed-point-free order 5.
checked: partial: unsatisfiable SAT claims carry DRAT proofs checked by drat-trim; a hand lemma covers order-4 types with one 4-cycle; enumerations and orbit-matrix searches not described as proof-checked

title: A Ramsey bound for Seidel switches of claw-free graphs
field: Ramsey theory, Seidel switching, claw-free graphs
problem: Every 43-vertex graph Seidel-switching-equivalent to a claw-free graph contains a K5 or an independent 5-set, and the induced Ramsey-good subgraphs of such switches have at most 42 vertices.
method: Double counting of length-two paths by centre across the switching cut, where cross edges have at most five and cross non-edges at most six common neighbours, giving an upper bound 2772 that contradicts a lower bound 5715/2 from degree, R(4,5)=25 and Caro-Wei.
checked: no: prose proof; supplement holds a bound-check script (not opened)

title: Rational, local, global and completion conditions for the local graph of an srg(45,22,10,11)
field: Ramsey theory, integral lattices, quadratic forms, strongly regular graphs
problem: For nonsingular positive definite F = 11I+10J-X-X^2, the rational condition is equivalent to all-one p-adic factors at every prime and to an odd unimodular lattice with characteristic centroid, and every known K4-free candidate with independence number at most 4 fails it.
method: Hasse-Minkowski and Witt cancellation reduce the rational class of the Gram matrix to local and lattice tests, and explicit 22x22 witness matrices with exact certificates separate the layers of conditions.
checked: partial: witnesses checked by a self-contained exact-arithmetic checker (named in abstract, not opened); main theorem proved by hand

title: Completion of singular local factors of an srg(45,22,10,11)
field: Ramsey theory, strongly regular graphs, Moore-Penrose inverse, switching
problem: At a singular root, the completions of a fixed 0/1 factor are C+T with T on the kernel satisfying T^2+T=11P; a corank-2 factor has at most two completions, differing by one switch that a (5,5)-good graph's K5 excludes.
method: Moore-Penrose projection identities reduce completion to a finite search for symmetric T on ker M, and at corank 2 the difference of two completions is forced to be a Wang-Qiu-Hu switch.

title: Marked C3-Equivariant Gluing Exclusions for H24_306763 and A21 at Orders 42 and 43 via Positive-Weight Triangle Conservation
field: Ramsey theory, equivariant SAT encodings, two-block gluing
problem: Excludes C3-equivariant gluings of the marked source H24_306763 at orders 42 and 43, of A21 at order 43, and of A21 at order 42 under the positive-weight hypothesis Family P.
method: Equivariant propositional encoding of 3x3 circulant cross-blocks, a triangle double-count bound on positive weights, and cube-and-conquer over Row-0 weight multisets, with each cube certified UNSAT by proof traces.

title: Solvable automorphism groups of hypothetical (5,5,45)-graphs
field: Ramsey theory, finite group theory, orbit arguments
problem: Every good graph on 45 vertices has a solvable automorphism group of order 2^a 3^b 5^e with e at most 1, conditional on the stated imported results.
method: A minimal nonsolvable subgroup argument with Frattini kernel over A5, orbital obstruction counting on odd orbits, a total-translation argument for smaller orbits, and the degree bound from R(4,5)=25.
checked: no: prose proof; imports a simple-group classification and computational Ramsey results and reports no new computation (per paper)

title: Normal five-subgroups in hypothetical (5,5,45)-graphs
field: Ramsey theory, finite group theory, row separation
problem: If 5 divides |Aut| of a good graph on 45 vertices, its Sylow 5-subgroup is normal and |Aut| = 2^a 3^eta 5 with eta at most 1.
method: Row separation between actual adjacency rows bounds 3-subgroups normalised by a free 5-element, and a commutator argument with the Ramsey degree window produces a forbidden five-clique in the 20+20+5 action.
checked: no: prose proof; no new numerical search (per paper)

title: Three-subgroups of Ramsey graph automorphism groups at orders 43-45
problem: Every three-subgroup of Aut of a good graph on 43, 44 or 45 vertices has order at most 9, so the 3-part of |Aut| is at most 9.
method: Exclusion of faithful actions of each of the five groups of order 27, with fixed-vertex and triangle-cut arguments for small orbits and a count of 27 attachment rows against at most 18 shared blue transversals for the nonabelian exponent-three group.
checked: no: prose proof; imports R(4,5)=25 as a computed result and reports no new enumeration (per paper)

title: Complete Exclusion of Faithful Cyclic Order-9 (C9) Automorphisms on (5,5)-Ramsey Graphs at Orders 42 to 45
problem: No (5,5,N) graph with N in 42 to 45 has an automorphism of order 9 with cycle type 9^n9 3^n3 1^n1, over all 125 partitions.
method: Analytic bounds on the fixed set of g^3 and hereditary deletion of short orbits reduce the partitions to 10 roots, and a pair-orbit SAT encoding with block-circulant normalizer canonicalization refutes the 2,712 canonical tuples with RUP-checked certificates.

title: Complete Exclusion of the n6 <= 1 Sector and Subgroup-Fixed Exterior Deficit Theory for Faithful Cyclic Order-6 (C6) Automorphisms on (5,5)-Ramsey Graphs at Orders 42 to 45
problem: Faithful C6 actions on (5,5,N) graphs with N in 42 to 45 need at least two regular 6-orbits, and 1,751 of 2,093 faithful partitions are excluded.
method: Short-orbit deletion and fixed-set bounds reduce the partitions to 251 minimal roots, which are refuted by a pair-orbit CNF with mixed-orbit normalizer canonicalization and PicoSAT extended RUP traces verified in memory, plus hand deficit arguments on Fix(g^2) and Fix(g^3).

title: Complete Exclusion of Faithful C3 x C3 Automorphisms at Orders 42 to 45 and Non-Divisibility of the Order of Aut(G) by 9 for (5,5)-Ramsey Graphs
problem: No (5,5,N) graph with N in 42 to 45 has a faithful C3 x C3 action, which excludes all 178 orbit-size triples and gives 9 does not divide the order of Aut(G) at those orders.
method: Slope-capacity and cross-slope clique, rectangle and block inequalities on one regular 9-orbit with its short orbits close the n9 = 1 and 2 cases by hand, and quotient-mask SAT encodings with RUP refutations close the remaining orbit triples.

title: Mixed (3,3,5) extensions of the 656 known Ramsey (5,5,42) graphs
problem: Classifies the one-vertex mixed (3,3,5) extensions of the 656 known good 42-vertex graphs: three catalogue bases, 17 labelled red neighbourhoods and 14 merged graphs up to isomorphism.
method: Each catalogue base is encoded as a SAT instance with triangle-free source-colour clauses, the measured blue neighbourhood is blocked to enumerate the remaining solutions, and each unsatisfiable input is certified by DRAT-trim.

title: The minimum number of monochromatic five-cliques under red-edge deletions in Exoo's cyclic colouring
problem: The minimum number of monochromatic K5s obtained by changing red edges of Exoo's Cyclic(43) is two, with 86 labelled minimizers, and at least three when blue edges are changed to red.
method: Unit edges are rescaled by 5 mod 43 so that every minimizer becomes an interval, and a count r+2q over interval endpoints gives a short case analysis, backed by a finite forcing check over 430 single and 92,235 double additions.
location: Sections 'Which red edges can change?', 'Counting five-cliques in a cyclic binary word', 'Why the deleted edges form one interval' (md lines 24-81)

title: Gluing critical thirteen-sets in mixed Ramsey colourings
field: Ramsey graphs, graph gluing and homomorphisms
problem: Mixed (3,3,5) colourings whose source colour maps to a triangle-free graph on at most 13 vertices have order at most 39, and at order 41 or more each triangle-free image has at least 16 vertices.
method: Critical 13-vertex sets are glued on a shared seven-vertex core, the gluing pattern reduces to bipartiteness of an index graph, and fractional colouring certificates over the 392 maximal triangle-free graphs on 13 vertices bound the homomorphic images.

title: Disjoint four-clique transversals at a pair of vertices in Ramsey (5,5) graphs
problem: Of 893 graph types on 27 vertices derived from the catalogue, exactly four admit the disjoint transversals needed for the prescribed 42-vertex colouring, and all 24 catalogue placements of those types fail to complete.
method: Exhaustive enumeration of catalogue-derived graphs on the 27 non-root vertices, a finite search for two disjoint six-element transversals of red four-cliques, and a forced red triangle argument (Proposition 3) for each original placement.

title: Opposite blue triangles with a common supporter in Ramsey (5,5) colourings
problem: Two inequivalent good 39-vertex colourings have a blue edge with 13 common blue and 15 common red neighbours and a common supporter, while none of the 2,524 relevant catalogue pairs at order 42 has one.
method: Completion between two blue cliques reduces to a permitted-crossing test bounded by a Konig matching identity, and the minimum-change lower bounds come from SAT instances whose DRAT refutations are checked.
location: Sections 'Completing the edges between two blue cliques', 'A rooted obstruction with arbitrary exterior vertices', 'Two realizations after changing the interior' (md lines 13-71)

title: A twelve-vertex induced pattern and one-defect sources for Ramsey (5,5) construction
problem: A 12-vertex induced pattern is absent from all 656 oriented order-42 catalogue graphs, and the 104 one-edge defect classes containing it give 164 good 41-vertex graphs whose largest extension with the 21 shared neighbourhoods has order 41.
method: An induced-embedding search with domain pruning over catalogue hosts, plus enumeration of single-edge recolourings through the fact that any new monochromatic five must contain the recoloured pair, with nauty canonical certificates identifying classes.

title: Common red neighbourhoods on the unique five-clique of a Ramsey colouring
problem: In a colouring with exactly one red K5 and no blue K5, the saturated edges of that five have maximum degree two, and a cycle of five saturated edges forces all overlaps to have size three.
method: Counting of common red neighbourhoods on the single red five, with case splits by overlap multiplicity profile, checked against the complete order-24 (4,5) catalogue and repaired by recolouring individual diagonals.

title: Sharp orbit cutoffs, alternating-group exclusion, and boundary realizations for the diagonal Ramsey problem R(5,5)
problem: A4, S4 and A5 are excluded as automorphism subgroups at every order from 38 onward, the A4 stratum cutoffs are 37, 37, 35 and 34, and C6 and S3 actions at orders 42 to 45 need at least four and two regular orbits.
method: Hereditary orbit deletion to minimal orbit tuples, exact rational capacity certificates for coset-fibre counts, and SAT refutations with RUP proofs over canonical symmetry representatives.

title: Exclusion of faithful 2^a*3 (a>=2) automorphism actions at orders 42 to 45 and extremal order-40 realizations for R(5,5)
problem: No group of order 2^a times 3 with a at least 2 acts faithfully on a (K5,I5)-free graph of order 42 to 45, and the sharp maximum order for an SL(2,3) action is 40.
method: A minimal-subgroup reduction cuts the groups to six minimal targets, and 6,184 minimal faithful roots are refuted by SAT proofs after row-canonical symmetry breaking, each checked by reverse unit propagation.

title: Neighbourhoods of a (4,5,22) graph with 110 edges and few codegree-4 edges
problem: The statement H114 (no (4,5,22) graph with 110 edges has every vertex on at most two codegree-4 edges) is proved for 10-regular graphs and three degree patterns, conditional on McKay's (3,5,10) and (3,5,11) lists being complete, and pattern (0,3,16,3) is narrowed.
method: Each vertex link is a (3,5,d) graph, so the codegree-4 count at a vertex equals the number of degree-4 vertices in its link, and SAT instances rooted at a fixed catalogue link are refuted with DRAT proofs checked by drat-trim.
